samples.summary: `useEffect(stay, [location, stay])` runs after children's effects, so a prompt raised by a child effect in the same commit is wiped immediately
samples.evidence: The provider itself documents (lines 77-80) that "React runs a child's effects before its parent's" and mirrors `location` during render for exactly that reason. The new auto-stay effect at line 174 ignores the same ordering: on any commit where `location` changed, every child effect runs first, and only then does `stay()` run, nulling `pendingRef` and `setPrompt(null)`. A child that issues a guarded `push` from a mount/update effect in that commit (a redirect rendered as `<Navigate to=... />` without `replace`, e.g. PrivateRoute.tsx:32, or any `navigate()` inside a `useEffect`) will have its prompt raised and then silently destroyed in the same commit — the navigation neither happens nor is offered to the user; the click/redirect is swallowed with no UI at all. The effect cannot distinguish "the app navigated past this prompt" from "this prompt was just created during this commit".

samples.summary: `basenamed` does not reproduce react-router's join for the root pathname, so the same-page exemption breaks at `/` under a basename
samples.evidence: react-router's `useNavigate` does `path.pathname = path.pathname === "/" ? basename : joinPaths([basename, path.pathname])` — for the root it uses the basename verbatim, with no trailing slash. `basenamed("/app", "/")` returns `["/app", "/"].join("/")` = "/app//" -> "/app/", which never equals the "/app" that `pathOf` sees for a push to "/". With `VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME` set (App.tsx:95), a search-only/state-only navigation while the user is at the app root is therefore classified as `leaving` and will raise the prompt even though the page is not being left. The `next === ""` early return at line 113 does not cover it, because `resolveTo` never yields an empty pathname.

samples.summary: The auto-stay effect fires on same-page location changes too, silently discarding the user's pending navigation
samples.evidence: The effect keys on any `location` identity change, but `leaving()` deliberately lets same-page navigations (query/state rewrites, e.g. `setSearchParams` in workspace-documents.tsx:77, or a `<Link to="/s/doc-1?tab=2">`) through unprompted. When one of those lands while a dialog is open, the location object changes, `stay()` runs, and the dialog vanishes along with `pendingRef` — the user's earlier click is dropped without them answering anything, even though they never left the page the dialog was describing. The comment at lines 169-173 only justifies clearing when the app has actually left the page.

samples.summary: The premise behind leaving `replace` unguarded is false: the app's auth redirects use push `<Navigate>`, so they are routed through the guard
samples.evidence: navigation-guard-provider.tsx:148-155 justifies guarding only `push` on the claim that app-initiated redirects — "`PrivateRoute` sending you to /login" — are `replace`. They are not: `PrivateRoute.tsx:32` renders `<Navigate to="/login" />` and `PublicRoute.tsx:21` renders `<Navigate to="/" />`, both without `replace`, and `<Navigate>` calls `navigate()` from an effect, i.e. `navigator.push`. If that redirect fires while a guard is still registered, it hits the guarded path and a "Stay" swallows it permanently — precisely the stranding failure the comment says the push/replace split avoids. It only escapes today by depending on React running the deleted editor subtree's passive cleanup (which unregisters the guard) before `<Navigate>`'s effect in the same commit — an ordering the code neither states nor enforces.
searchedFor: grep for <Navigate / replace: true across packages/frontend/src

finding.summary: `useEffect(stay, [location, stay])` runs after children's effects, so a prompt raised by a child effect in the same commit is wiped immediately
finding.evidence: The provider itself documents (lines 77-80) that "React runs a child's effects before its parent's" and mirrors `location` during render for exactly that reason. The new auto-stay effect at line 174 ignores the same ordering: on any commit where `location` changed, every child effect runs first, and only then does `stay()` run, nulling `pendingRef` and `setPrompt(null)`. A child that issues a guarded `push` from a mount/update effect in that commit (a redirect rendered as `<Navigate to=... />` without `replace`, e.g. PrivateRoute.tsx:32, or any `navigate()` inside a `useEffect`) will have its prompt raised and then silently destroyed in the same commit — the navigation neither happens nor is offered to the user; the click/redirect is swallowed with no UI at all. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: navigation-guard-provider.tsx:174 runs `useEffect(stay, [location, stay])`, and `stay` (lines 164-167) unconditionally clears `pendingRef` and the prompt with no check of which location the prompt belongs to. The file's own comment at lines 77-80 establishes that React runs child effects before the parent's, so in any commit where `location` changed (or on provider mount) a prompt raised by a child effect via the guarded `push` path (lines 118-135, which stores `run` in `pendingRef` and returns without navigating) is nulled out afterwards — losing both the dialog and the pending navigation. PrivateRoute.tsx:32 is correctly quoted: `<Navigate to="/login" />` with no `replace`, i.e. a push issued from an effect, unlike the other redirects (file-detail.tsx:242/247, document-detail.tsx:863, docs-detail.tsx:342) which do pass `replace`. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable: the sole registration site (sync-status-chip.tsx:115 -> use-navigation-guard.ts:54-57) registers globally with no location scoping, and the tests only cover the intended prompt-then-navigate direction (navigation-guard.test.tsx:172-184). I could not construct a definitive concrete trigger — the app's in-effect redirects I enumerated (document-detail.tsx:229, docs-detail.tsx:162, file-shell.tsx:73) all use `replace`, and the PrivateRoute Navigate path probably unmounts the guard-owning subtree in the same commit — but inability to build a trigger is not a refutation ground, so the finding stands. No named refutation ground applies: not-present fails (code is there), already-guarded fails (no such guard), out-of-scope fails (swallowed navigation / destroyed pending state is core correctness).

verdict.reason: Every factual claim checks out in the repository. navigation-guard-provider.tsx:148-155 justifies guarding only `push` on the explicit premise that the app's own redirects are `replace`, naming "`PrivateRoute` sending you to /login"; `replace` is passed through unguarded at line 158 while `push` runs the guard loop (lines 118-135, wired at 157). But PrivateRoute.tsx:32 renders `<Navigate to="/login" />` and PublicRoute.tsx:21 renders `<Navigate to="/" />`, both without `replace`, so both resolve to `navigator.push` and enter the guarded path. The test suite encodes the same false premise (navigation-guard.test.tsx:51-54 comment "The app's own redirects ... are all `replace`" and the `<Link to="/login" replace>` harness at :53, asserted at :159-170), so no test covers the real redirect. I could not refute on reachability: the sole guard registrant (sync-status-chip.tsx:115 via use-navigation-guard.ts:54-57) does sit inside PrivateRoute's Outlet branch (App.tsx:128-176), which is mutually exclusive with the Navigate branch, but the only thing preventing a held redirect is React's passive unmount-before-mount ordering plus `<Navigate>` using a passive effect - both external library internals (node_modules absent from this tree, react-router-dom ^7.18.2 per packages/frontend/package.json), and nothing in this repository states or enforces that ordering. If it does not hold, a "Stay" clears pendingRef (lines 164-167) and swallows the auth redirect permanently while `<Navigate>` renders nothing, a broken core flow; separately the missing `replace` pushes a history entry so Back returns to the protected route and redirects again. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: The guard intercepts automatic/programmatic redirects, not just user-initiated navigation; choosing "Stay" cancels such a redirect permanently
finding.evidence: Every `navigate()` goes through the patched `navigator.push/replace`, including redirects the user never asked for. `document-detail.tsx:229` (`if (isDocumentError) { toast.error('Document not found'); navigate(fallback, {replace:true}) }`, and the identical effects at docs-detail.tsx:162, notes-detail.tsx:183, slides-detail.tsx:161, board-detail.tsx:125, file-shell.tsx:73) fires while the chip is mounted; if `hasUnsentEdits()` is true at that instant the redirect is held behind the dialog. `stay()` (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:141) discards `pendingRef` and nothing retries — the effect's deps (`isDocumentError`, `navigate`, `fallbackSlug`) do not change again — so the user is left sitting on a document that failed to load with the recovery redirect silently dropped. Same shape for the auth redirects `<Navigate to="/login" replace />` (PrivateRoute.tsx:32, document-detail.tsx:863, docs-detail.tsx:342, notes-detail.tsx:369, slides-detail.tsx:947, board-detail.tsx:252): a session expiry mid-edit can be blocked by a dialog rendered over a route that has already returned `null`, and "Stay" leaves a blank screen with no way forward (lower confidence here, since it depends on whether the chip's passive unregister runs before `<Navigate>`'s effect in the same commit).

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that programmatic/automatic redirects pass through the patched navigator's guard — is false. The provider guards ONLY `push`; `replace` is an unmodified pass-through (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:158, with the design rationale spelled out at :148-155 naming these exact 404-fallback and /login cases). Every redirect the finding cites uses `replace`: document-detail.tsx:229-231, docs-detail.tsx:162-164, notes-detail.tsx:183-185, slides-detail.tsx:161-163, board-detail.tsx:125-127, file-shell.tsx:73 all pass `{ replace: true }`, and the auth redirects document-detail.tsx:863, docs-detail.tsx:342, notes-detail.tsx:369, slides-detail.tsx:947, board-detail.tsx:252 are all `<Navigate to="/login" replace />`. None reach the guard loop, so none can be held behind the dialog or dropped by `stay()`. The single site that does use push, PrivateRoute.tsx:32 (`<Navigate to="/login" />`, misquoted by the finding as `replace`), is unreachable with a registered guard: the only registrant is SyncStatusChip (sync-status-chip.tsx:115 -> use-navigation-guard.ts:54-57), which renders inside the `<Outlet/>` branch (PrivateRoute.tsx:22-30); flipping to the Navigate branch unmounts it in the same commit, and React flushes passive unmount cleanups before the new `<Navigate>`'s passive mount effect, so the guard set is already empty. PrivateRoute also reads `data: me`, which react-query retains across a failed background refetch, so the branch does not flip mid-edit.
